_comment: Why each repertoire move is played. Key: the SAN moves from the start up to and including the move. note: the idea, in neutral White/Black voice. cue: for moves the player must find, a hint that points at the idea without naming the move. See build/explain.py.

Nf3.note: White develops a knight first, keeping options open. It controls e5 and d4 and waits to see Black's setup.

b3.note: White prepares to fianchetto the dark bishop on b2, aiming at the centre from the side.

c4.note: White starts on the flank, controlling d5 from the side and keeping the centre pawns flexible.

d4.note: White puts a pawn in the centre, controls e5 and c5, and frees the queen and the dark-squared bishop.
d4.cue: Start by claiming the centre with a pawn — the queen's pawn this time.

e3.note: White opens the f1-bishop with a modest pawn move, taking only a small share of the centre.

e4.note: White grabs the centre with a pawn and opens lines for the queen and the f1-bishop, ready to develop quickly.
e4.cue: Claim the centre with a pawn and free your kingside bishop.

Nf3 d5.note: Black takes a share of the centre right away with a pawn, instead of letting the flank opening dictate the game.
Nf3 d5.cue: Occupy the centre with a pawn.

b3 e5.note: Black takes the centre with a pawn. White will hit it with Bb2, but it is easy to defend.
b3 e5.cue: Occupy the centre with a pawn.

c4 e5.note: Black takes a big share of the centre right away instead of copying White's flank play.
c4 e5.cue: Occupy the centre with a pawn that also frees a bishop.

d4 Nf6.note: Black develops first, controls e4, and keeps the choice of pawn setup open.

d4 d5.note: Black matches White in the centre, stopping White from playing e4 for free and opening a path for the light bishop.
d4 d5.cue: Meet White's centre pawn with one of your own, side by side.

e3 e5.note: Black takes the centre with a big pawn and frees the f8-bishop. Against a quiet first move, Black can claim the middle for free.
e3 e5.cue: Grab the centre with a pawn that also frees a bishop.

e4 c5.note: Black fights for the d4-square from the side instead of copying White's centre pawn. This leads to unbalanced positions.

e4 c6.note: Black prepares ...d5 next, challenging e4 with a pawn backed up by the c-pawn. Solid, and the light-squared bishop stays free.
e4 c6.cue: Prepare to strike the centre next move, using a pawn that will back it up.

e4 d5.note: Black strikes at White's e4-pawn straight away, threatening to take it. White usually captures, and Black recaptures — even with the queen — to fight for the centre.

e4 d6.note: Black controls e5 and frees the c8-bishop, letting White build a centre and planning to attack it later.

e4 e5.note: Black claims an equal share of the centre and opens the way for the f8-bishop and the queen.
e4 e5.cue: Answer White's central pawn with one of your own, side by side.

e4 e6.note: Black prepares ...d5 to challenge White's centre with pawn support, and opens the f8-bishop.

e4 g6.note: Black prepares to put the bishop on g7 and lets White build a centre, planning to attack it later with pieces and pawn breaks.

Nf3 d5 d4.note: White heads into a normal queen's-pawn position, putting a second pawn in the centre.

Nf3 d5 g3.note: White gets ready to put the bishop on g2, where it will aim down the long diagonal at the centre.

b3 e5 Bb2.note: White develops the bishop with gain of time, attacking the e5-pawn.

c4 e5 b4.note: A wing gambit: White offers the b-pawn to get Bb2 in quickly, aiming at e5. Black can take for free.

d4 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops and controls e5. The London setup (Bf4, e3, c3) works against almost anything Black does.
d4 Nf6 Nf3.cue: Develop a kingside piece toward the centre.

d4 d5 Bf4.note: An early London: White brings the dark bishop out before e3 or Nf3.

d4 d5 Nc3.note: White brings the knight out early (a Jobava-style setup), adding pressure on d5 and often following with Bf4 and Nb5 ideas.

d4 d5 Nf3.note: White develops and controls e5, keeping options open for setups like Bf4/e3 or c4.
d4 d5 Nf3.cue: Develop a kingside piece toward the centre.

d4 d5 c4.note: White offers the c-pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre; if Black takes, White can usually win the pawn back and build a big centre with e4.
d4 d5 c4.cue: Challenge Black's centre pawn from the side with a wing pawn.

d4 d5 e3.note: A quiet setup (Colle-style): White supports d4 and frees the f1-bishop, but the c1-bishop is shut in.

e3 e5 Qh5.note: An early queen raid: White threatens Qxe5+ and eyes f7. It breaks the rule of developing minor pieces first, and the queen will get chased.

e4 c5 c3.note: White prepares to play d4 and build a full pawn centre; if Black exchanges on d4, the c-pawn recaptures and keeps two centre pawns.
e4 c5 c3.cue: Prepare to put a second pawn in the centre, so you can recapture with a pawn if it's taken.

e4 c6 Bc4.note: White aims the bishop at f7 for a quick attack, but the bishop is exposed to ...d5.

e4 c6 Nc3.note: White develops and keeps options open; Black still answers with ...d5.

e4 c6 Nf3.note: White develops and leaves e4 to be defended later; Black continues with ...d5.

e4 c6 Qf3.note: An early queen sortie eyeing f7, but f7 is safely guarded by the king. Black ignores it and takes the centre.

e4 c6 d3.note: A passive start: White supports e4 and opens the c1-bishop, but gives Black a free hand in the centre.

e4 c6 d4.note: White takes the full centre with two pawns side by side, the most natural reply.
e4 c6 d4.cue: Black hasn't challenged yet: grab more of the centre with a pawn.

e4 d5 exd5.note: White takes the pawn that attacked e4. Black must now spend a move winning it back, often bringing the queen out early where it can be chased.
e4 d5 exd5.cue: A pawn is attacking your e-pawn. Remove it.

e4 d6 d4.note: White takes the centre with a second pawn and opens the c1-bishop.
e4 d6 d4.cue: Black is passive — take more central space with a pawn.

e4 e5 Bc4.note: White develops the bishop to its active diagonal, aiming at f7, the weakest point near Black's king.

e4 e5 Nc3.note: White develops a knight that guards e4 and eyes d5, keeping the f-pawn free to advance later.
e4 e5 Nc3.cue: Develop a queenside piece that protects your e-pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3.note: White develops a knight with tempo: it attacks the e5-pawn, so Black must react, and it clears the way to castle.
e4 e5 Nf3.cue: Develop a kingside piece that also attacks the e5-pawn.

e4 e5 Qf3.note: Another early queen move: White eyes f7 and plans Bc4 for a mating attack. It also blocks the g1-knight's natural square.

e4 e5 Qh5.note: An early queen sortie: White attacks e5 (Qxe5+ is a threat) and eyes f7, hoping for a quick Scholar's Mate with Bc4. The queen will be chased with tempo.

e4 e5 d3.note: A quiet, passive move: White guards e4 and frees the c1-bishop but gives up any claim to d4 for now. Black can take the centre freely.

e4 e5 d4.note: White opens the centre right away, attacking e5. The catch: if Black takes, White's queen recaptures early and can be chased.

e4 e5 f4.note: A gambit: White offers the f-pawn to deflect Black's e-pawn, hoping to build a centre with d4 and open the f-file.

e4 e6 d4.note: White builds the ideal pawn centre while Black's move doesn't stop it.
e4 e6 d4.cue: Take more of the centre with your other central pawn.

e4 g6 d4.note: White takes a full pawn centre while Black is not contesting it, and opens the c1-bishop.
e4 g6 d4.cue: Black isn't fighting for the centre. Take more central space with a pawn.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to its best square, guarding d5 and e4.
Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that protects your centre pawn.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5.note: Black grabs more space and controls d4, aiming for a broad centre with ...Nc6, ...Nf6 and ...e6.
Nf3 d5 g3 c5.cue: Take more space with a wing pawn that also controls a key centre square.

b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6.note: Black defends e5 by developing a piece.
b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6.cue: Protect your attacked centre pawn by developing a piece.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4.note: Black takes the free pawn while developing the bishop. The pawn is safe and White has little to show for it.
c4 e5 b4 Bxb4.cue: White's offered pawn can be taken by a piece that wants to develop anyway.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5.note: Black puts a pawn in the centre, blocking any early e4 by White.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6.note: Black prepares to fianchetto the dark bishop on g7, a King's Indian-style setup.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5.note: Black strikes at d4 right away, before White is comfortable. With the bishop gone from c1, b2 may become a target too.
d4 d5 Bf4 c5.cue: Hit White's d-pawn with a wing pawn before they get comfortable.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6.note: Black develops the knight to its natural square and hits d4 straight back.
d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6.cue: Develop your queenside knight so it hits White's d-pawn.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to its natural square, guarding d5 and controlling e4.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece toward the centre.

d4 d5 c4 c6.note: Black holds the d5-pawn with another pawn. Unlike ...e6, this keeps the c8-bishop free to come out to f5 or g4 later.
d4 d5 c4 c6.cue: Support your centre pawn with a pawn — but keep your light bishop's diagonal open.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4.note: Black takes the c4-pawn, giving up the centre for now but planning to hit back with ...c5 or ...e5. Black usually doesn't try to keep the pawn.

d4 d5 c4 e6.note: Black supports d5 with the e-pawn: very solid, though the c8-bishop is now shut in for a while.

d4 d5 e3 e6.note: Black mirrors with a solid setup, opening the f8-bishop and holding d5.
d4 d5 e3 e6.cue: Answer quietly: free your dark bishop and back up your centre pawn.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6.note: Black defends e5 by developing a piece. The queen out on h5 will soon become a target.
e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6.cue: Protect your attacked centre pawn by developing a piece.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6.note: Black attacks the e4-pawn right away. Because c3 took the knight's natural square, White can't defend it with Nc3.

e4 c5 c3 d5.note: Black hits e4 at once, before White can play d4 and support it. Taking on d5 lets Black's queen recapture, since Nc3 is not available.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5.note: The punishment: Black's d-pawn hits both the bishop and e4 at once, threatening dxc4.
e4 c6 Bc4 d5.cue: Hit the bishop and the e4-pawn with one pawn move.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5.note: Black follows the standard plan, attacking e4 with a pawn backed by c6.
e4 c6 Nc3 d5.cue: Stick to the plan: challenge e4 with a supported pawn.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5.note: Black hits e4 at once; it is not defended, so White must guard it, trade, or push.
e4 c6 Nf3 d5.cue: Attack the e4-pawn with a pawn that the c6-pawn supports.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5.note: Black takes the centre; the queen on f3 blocks White's natural knight square, so ...dxe4 can even gain time on it.
e4 c6 Qf3 d5.cue: Ignore the queen and challenge e4 with a supported pawn.

e4 c6 d3 d5.note: Black takes the centre as usual; against a slow d3 Black can aim for ...e5 too.
e4 c6 d3 d5.cue: White played slowly — challenge e4 with a supported pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5.note: The point of 1...c6: Black hits e4, and if White trades on d5 the c-pawn recaptures, keeping a pawn in the centre.
e4 c6 d4 d5.cue: Attack the e4-pawn with a pawn that the c6-pawn supports.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6.note: Black doesn't rush to take back with the queen; the knight will recapture on d5 instead, avoiding being chased around.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5.note: Black wins the pawn back with the queen. It stands well in the centre for now, but an early queen is a target White can gain time against.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6.note: Black develops and attacks e4, threatening to win it, so White needs to defend it.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6.note: Black develops and hits the e4-pawn, which nothing protects, so ...Nxe4 is already a threat.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that attacks White's undefended e-pawn.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops and puts pressure on e4, also eyeing ...d5 to free the position.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that pressures White's e-pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5.note: Black develops the bishop toward f2 but leaves e5 undefended, so White can simply take a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6.note: Black develops a knight and guards the e5-pawn that White's knight is attacking. The most natural reply: it fights for the centre and keeps options open.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6.note: Instead of defending e5, Black counterattacks e4 with a developing move. This is the Petrov idea: symmetry and solidity.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Don't defend your pawn; develop a piece that hits White's e-pawn instead.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6.note: Black defends e5 with the queen. It holds the pawn but takes the f6-square from Black's knight and puts the queen where it can be chased.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5.note: The Elephant Gambit: Black counterattacks e4 instead of defending e5. It's risky — after exd5 Black is a pawn down and e5 is still under attack.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6.note: Black defends e5 with a pawn — the Philidor Defence. Solid but passive: it shuts in the f8-bishop, so White should grab the centre and develop fast.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6.note: Black develops, blocks the queen's f-file toward f7, and hits e4.
e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that blocks the queen's line to f7.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6.note: Black defends e5 with a developing move. The knight is better here than ...g6 at once, which would allow Qxe5+.
e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked: defend it while developing a piece.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6.note: Black develops toward the centre and eyes e4, preparing ...d5 to grab more space.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece toward the centre, eyeing White's e-pawn.

e4 e5 d4 exd4.note: Black takes the pawn. Now White has to recapture with the queen (or gambit it), and the queen in the centre becomes a target.
e4 e5 d4 exd4.cue: White's pawn is attacking yours: capture it.

e4 e5 f4 exf4.note: Black accepts the pawn. It also threatens ...Qh4+, a nasty check now that the f-pawn is gone.
e4 e5 f4 exf4.cue: White offers a pawn: accept it.

e4 e6 d4 d5.note: Black challenges e4 with the d-pawn, which is backed up by the e6-pawn. White must decide whether to defend, trade or push.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7.note: Black fianchettoes the bishop, which presses on d4 along the long diagonal.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3.note: White develops the knight in front of the c-pawn and adds pressure on d5, often with ideas of Bf4 or Bg5.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2.note: White develops the bishop onto the long diagonal, where it puts pressure on d5 and the queenside, and gets ready to castle.

b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3.note: White plans a second fianchetto with Bg2, a slow, flank-based setup.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2.note: White develops with gain of time, hitting the unprotected e5-pawn.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4.note: The London: White brings the dark bishop out before e3, so it is not stuck inside the pawn chain.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4.cue: Develop your dark-squared bishop before your e-pawn blocks it in.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.note: White sticks to the London plan: the dark bishop comes out before e3 can lock it in.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4.cue: Get your dark bishop outside the pawn chain before playing your next pawn move.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3.note: White supports d4 with a pawn and opens the f1-bishop.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4.note: The London: White brings the dark bishop out before e3 locks it in, and gets ready to build the e3/c3 pawn chain.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4.cue: Get your dark bishop out before your e-pawn closes it in.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3.note: White develops the knight in front of the c-pawn, adding pressure on d5 and hinting at e4 later.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3.note: White develops the queenside knight, adding pressure on d5 and getting ready for e4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3.note: White develops, guards d4 and stops ...e5, keeping the pressure on the centre.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3.cue: Bring out a kingside piece that also guards your d-pawn.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5.note: White goes for the Exchange Slav: a symmetrical, open c-file structure. Black has to recapture now, or dxc6 wins a pawn.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3.note: White develops and stops ...e5, which would challenge the centre, before winning back c4.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3.cue: Develop a piece that stops Black from hitting back in the centre with the e-pawn.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3.note: White develops and adds pressure on d5, getting ready for Bg5 to pin the f6-knight.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3.cue: Develop your queenside knight to add pressure on d5.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4.note: White adds the bishop to the queen and threatens Qxf7#, the classic beginner's mate.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5.note: White pushes the pawn forward with tempo, chasing the knight and gaining space. The pawn on e5 also keeps Black's pieces off f6 and d6.
e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked. Gain space by pushing it and attacking the knight.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5.note: White takes the pawn. Black's queen will recapture, but with the c3-pawn in place it can't be chased by Nc3, so White plans d4 instead.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5.cue: An enemy pawn is attacking your e-pawn. Capture it.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5.note: White takes, removing the pawn that attacked the bishop and threatening dxc6.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5.note: White trades on d5, threatening dxc6, and hopes for quick piece play.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3.note: White defends e4 by developing (the Two Knights set-up).

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3.note: White guards e4 with the bishop but blocks the d-pawn, so White's queenside stays stuck.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2.note: An odd developing move that doesn't fight for the centre, so Black grabs more space.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3.note: White defends e4 with a developing move — the main line. Black usually takes on e4 next.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2.note: White defends e4 with the knight, keeping the c-pawn free. Black usually takes on e4 next.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5.note: The Advance: White gains space and cramps Black's kingside knight, but gives up pressure on d5.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5.note: The Exchange: White trades the centre pawns, aiming for quick, simple development. It also threatens dxc6.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5.cue: Release the tension in the centre with a capture.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4.note: White ignores the attack on d5 and builds the centre. Black can win the pawn back with the knight, but White is left with a strong pawn on d4.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4.cue: Don't hang on to the extra pawn — build your centre and free your bishop.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3.note: White develops with tempo: the knight hits the undefended queen, which must move again, so White gets ahead in development.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3.cue: Develop a piece that attacks the enemy queen in the centre.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3.note: White develops while guarding e4, the most natural way to meet the threat.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked. Defend it while developing a piece.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops and counterattacks e5 instead of defending e4. Both centre pawns are now loose, and White hopes the bishop on c4 gives play against f7.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3.note: White defends e4 with the queen and lines it up with the bishop against f7. The knight on f6 blocks that for now, but the early queen can be chased.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4.note: White aims the bishop at f7, keeping the option of f4 later.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4.cue: Develop your kingside bishop to its most active diagonal.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops naturally, attacking e5 and clearing the way to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5.note: White takes the free pawn. The knight is strong on e5 and eyes f7.
e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5.cue: Black's e5-pawn has no defender — take it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.note: White develops and attacks the c6-knight, the defender of e5. It's not an immediate threat, but the pressure on e5 lasts all game. The Ruy Lopez.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5.cue: Develop a bishop so that it attacks the knight that guards Black's e5-pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.note: White develops the bishop to its best diagonal, aiming at f7 — the weakest point near Black's king — and gets ready to castle. The Italian Game.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.cue: Develop a bishop to a diagonal that aims at Black's weak f7-square.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4.note: White strikes the centre at once, attacking e5 a second time. The Scotch: White opens lines early and aims for quick, easy development.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4.cue: Attack Black's e5-pawn again — with a pawn, right in the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4.note: White develops the bishop toward f7 but leaves e4 undefended, so Black can take it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3.note: White defends e4 with a developing move instead of grabbing on e5. It is a calm, natural set-up that avoids the sharp Petrov lines.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5.note: White takes the pawn at once. The knight on e5 now eyes f7, and Black has to be careful how to win the pawn back.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5.cue: Take the pawn that your opponent left undefended.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3.note: White simply defends e4. It is passive, but now Nxe5 really wins a pawn, since ...Nxe4 is no longer possible.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4.note: White opens the centre at once (the Steinitz idea): the d-pawn joins the fight for e5 and opens the queen's line.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4.note: White develops toward f7 and gets ready to castle. Black's queen on f6 isn't doing much, so White simply develops.
e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4.cue: Develop a bishop toward f7 and get ready to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5.note: White simply takes the pawn. Black's e5-pawn is still attacked, so White is already doing well.
e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5.cue: Black offered a pawn — take it.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4.note: White strikes the centre with a pawn, attacking e5 again. Keep the tension and develop; trading with dxe5 early usually helps Black.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4.cue: Black's play is passive — challenge e5 with a pawn and claim the centre.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4.note: White adds the bishop to the pressure on f7, but the knight on f6 holds that line shut.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4.note: White adds the bishop to the attack on f7: Qxf7 is now checkmate unless Black does something.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5.note: White develops and pins the f6-knight to the queen. It is annoying but not dangerous; Black just keeps developing.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3.note: An odd square for the knight: from h3 it can jump to g5, but it is far from the centre and can be hit by the c8-bishop.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4.note: White wins back the pawn, but the queen comes out early and Black can gain time by attacking it with a developing move.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5.note: White pushes past instead of recapturing, hoping to cramp Black's pieces, but this leaves e5 loose and lets Black keep the extra pawn for now.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3.note: White develops and covers h4, stopping ...Qh4+. White plans to regain the f4-pawn later.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5.note: White pushes past to gain space. The e5-pawn takes the f6-square from Black's knight and cramps Black's kingside.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked. Gain space instead of trading or defending.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3.note: White develops the knight, guards d4 against the g7-bishop and prepares to castle.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3.cue: Develop a piece that defends your d-pawn from the bishop's pressure.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.note: Black prepares to fianchetto the dark bishop on g7, where it will guard the castled king and aim at the centre along the long diagonal.
Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.cue: Make room for your dark bishop to go to the long diagonal.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6.note: Black develops, defends d5 and prepares to castle.
Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that defends your centre pawn.

b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3 d5.note: Black puts a second pawn in the centre, building a broad pawn centre while White sits on the flanks.
b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3 d5.cue: White is slow — build a full pawn centre.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6.note: Black solidly guards e5 with a pawn and opens the c8-bishop. Black stays a clean pawn up.
c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6.cue: Your centre pawn is attacked — protect it with a pawn and free your light bishop.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5.note: Black attacks d4 right away. This is the most testing plan against the London, aiming at b2 next with ...Qb6.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7.note: Black finishes the fianchetto. The bishop sits on the long diagonal behind the f6-knight and comes alive once the centre opens.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4.note: Black exchanges in the centre; White must recapture or lose a pawn.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops the other knight, guarding d5 and controlling e4.
d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Develop your other knight, guarding your centre pawn.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5.note: Black mirrors the London, bringing the light bishop out before ...e6 so it won't be shut in.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5.cue: Copy White's idea: get your light bishop outside before your e-pawn moves.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5.note: Black hits d4 at once, the most direct way to bother the London. The b2-pawn will be a target too.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6.note: Black prepares a kingside fianchetto, so the bishop on g7 will guard Black's king and aim along the long diagonal at the centre.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6.cue: Make room for your dark bishop on the long diagonal.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to its natural square, guarding d5 and keeping White from playing e4.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that guards your centre pawn and watches e4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to its best square, guarding d5 and the e4-square.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Develop the piece that also protects your centre pawn and watches e4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures with the c-pawn, keeping a pawn on d5 and a symmetrical, rock-solid centre.
d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5.cue: White took in the centre — recapture so you keep a pawn there.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops, controlling e4 and d5.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops and defends d5 again.

d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops, guarding d5 and controlling e4.
d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece toward the centre.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5.note: Black blocks the bishop's diagonal to f7, so mate is off, and attacks the bishop at the same time, gaining space and opening the c8-bishop.
e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5.cue: White is aiming at f7 — block the bishop's line with a pawn that also attacks it.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5.note: The knight goes to the strong central d5-square. Since White's own pawn sits on c3, White can't kick it with c4 in one move, so White develops instead.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5.note: Black recaptures with the queen, which is strong in the centre here because White's c3-pawn has taken the knight's best square.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures and attacks the bishop again, now threatening dxc4. White has lost time with the bishop.
e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5.cue: Recapture in a way that attacks White's bishop again.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures with the pawn and keeps a strong pawn in the centre.
e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5.cue: Recapture so that you keep a pawn in the centre.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4.note: Black develops the light bishop actively, pinning the f3-knight to the queen and loosening White's grip on e5 and d4.
e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4.cue: Develop your light bishop actively against the f3-knight.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5.note: Black builds a big pawn centre and frees the dark bishop; White's awkward set-up can't challenge it.
e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5.cue: White is passive — take more central space with a pawn.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5.note: Black builds a big pawn centre and frees the f8-bishop. White's slow set-up has handed Black the middle.
e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5.cue: White is passive — take more central space with a pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4.note: Black trades off White's e4-pawn, opening the way to develop the light bishop with tempo on the e4-knight.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4.cue: Remove White's e4-pawn so you can free your pieces.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4.note: Black removes the e4-pawn; with the knight on d2 blocking the queen, d4 is loose, so White must recapture at once.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4.cue: Remove White's e4-pawn so you can free your pieces.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5.note: Black brings the light bishop out BEFORE playing ...e6, so it isn't shut in behind the pawns. This is the key Caro-Kann idea.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5.cue: Get your light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before you lock it in.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures with the c-pawn, keeping a strong pawn on d5 and opening the c-file for later.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5.cue: Recapture so that you keep a pawn in the centre.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5.note: Black regains the pawn with the knight, which stands centrally on d5 but can later be hit by c4.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5.note: Black's queen escapes to a5, out of the way of White's pieces. From there it watches the c3-knight and the a5-e1 diagonal, and can combine with ...Bb4 later.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6.note: Black's queen retreats to d6 instead. It stays central and eyes h2, but can be hit again by Nb5 or Bf4 later.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6.note: Black prepares ...Bg7, where the bishop will press against White's centre on the long diagonal.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4.note: Black accepts and takes the pawn. The knight is active, and Black will answer White's Nxe5 with ...d5.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4.cue: White left a centre pawn hanging: take it.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5.note: Black hits back in the centre: the pawn attacks the c4-bishop, and opening lines suits Black, who is better developed than White's lone queen.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5.cue: Attack White's bishop with a central pawn and open lines for your pieces.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5.note: Black develops actively too, aiming at f2 and preparing to castle.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5.cue: Develop your kingside bishop to the diagonal pointing at White's weak f-pawn.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6.note: Black develops calmly and avoids the risky ...Nxe4 lines.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.note: Black grabs e4 with the 'fork trick' idea: if Nxe4, then ...d5 forks bishop and knight and wins the piece back. But it lets White's queen into the game.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.note: Black defends e5 with a developing move. All four knights are out: the Four Knights Game.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked: defend it while developing.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4.note: Black's queen hunts for counterplay: it threatens Qxf2 mate (with the bishop's help) and also attacks e4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6.note: Black develops and hits e4 right away instead of ...a6. This is the solid Berlin Defence.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6.note: Black asks the bishop a question right away. White can't win e5 yet (Bxc6 then Nxe5 runs into ...Qd4), so the bishop usually retreats.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.note: Black mirrors White: the bishop takes an active diagonal aimed at f2, and Black is ready to develop the kingside.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6.note: Black develops and counterattacks e4 instead of copying White. This is the Two Knights; White should defend calmly.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4.note: Black takes, because the e5-pawn was attacked twice and could not hold. Black gives up the centre pawn but gets White's d-pawn off the board.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.note: Black takes the free pawn. The knight is active, and if Nxe5 comes, Black blocks the bishop with ...d5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4.cue: White left the e-pawn undefended: take it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6.note: Black copies: develop the knight and defend e5. Now all four knights are out (the Four Knights Game).
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6.cue: Develop a queenside piece that also protects your e-pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4.note: Black copies White and grabs e4 at once — a known mistake. It walks into Qe2, where the knight is attacked and can't simply retreat.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6.note: Black kicks the knight first and only then takes on e4. Copying at once with ...Nxe4 is a known trap: after Qe2, the retreat ...Nf6?? loses the queen to Nc6+.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6.cue: Before grabbing back a pawn, first chase White's knight away with a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6.note: Black defends e5 with a developing move, stopping Nxe5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6.cue: Your e-pawn is now genuinely attacked: defend it with a developing move.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4.note: Black grabs the e4-pawn while it is undefended. The knight is active in the centre and Black will defend it with ...d5.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4.cue: One of White's centre pawns is loose: take it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4 Bc5.note: Black develops the bishop on its active diagonal toward f2.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6.note: Black develops instead of recapturing, hoping to win back d5 later. Meanwhile e5 is left undefended.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5.note: Black recaptures with the queen and wins the pawn back, but the queen is out early and can be chased with tempo.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4.note: Black gives up the centre to free the position. White recaptures and keeps a nice space advantage.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6.note: Black props up e5 with the f-pawn. It holds the centre, but takes f6 away from the knight and weakens the diagonal toward Black's king.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5.note: Black hits the bishop with a central pawn, opening lines while White has only the queen and bishop out.
e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5.cue: Attack White's bishop with a central pawn.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6.note: Black stops the mate threat by attacking the queen with a pawn. The queen must move, and the bishop can later go to g7.
e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6.cue: Mate is threatened on f7: kick the queen away with a pawn.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6.note: Black ignores the pin and develops, keeping ...d5 and ...h6 in reserve.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6.cue: Ignore the pin for now and develop another piece toward the centre.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5.note: Black takes the centre with a pawn and opens the c8-bishop's diagonal toward the knight on h3; ...Bxh3 would wreck White's kingside pawns.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5.cue: Grab the centre with a pawn that also opens your light-squared bishop's diagonal.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6.note: Black develops with tempo by attacking the queen, which has to move again.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6.cue: White's queen is in the centre: develop a piece that attacks it.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6.note: Black attacks the advanced e5-pawn right away and opens the c8-bishop.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6.cue: Strike at White's advanced e-pawn with a pawn.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6.note: Black develops and attacks the e4-pawn, which has no defender.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that attacks White's undefended e-pawn.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5.note: Black hits the base of White's pawn chain at d4 right away. This is Black's main way to fight the e5-d4 centre.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6.note: Black controls e5 so White can't easily push e4-e5, and opens the c8-bishop.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3.note: White plays a quiet setup, opening the f1-bishop and supporting d4.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O.note: White castles early. The king is safe behind the fianchetto before White starts any central play.

b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3 d5 Bg2.note: White aims the second bishop at d5, putting pressure on Black's centre.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3.note: White opens the f1-bishop and controls d4, continuing development.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3.note: White supports d4 with a pawn and opens the f1-bishop.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3.cue: Support your attacked d-pawn with a pawn.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3.note: White supports d4 and opens the f1-bishop, keeping a solid London structure.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3.cue: Support your d-pawn and open the way for your other bishop.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4.note: White recaptures toward the centre, keeping a pawn on d4 and opening the e-file and the f1-bishop.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 e3.note: White supports d4 and opens the f1-bishop, but the c1-bishop is now shut in.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3.note: White supports d4 and opens the f1-bishop.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3.note: White backs up d4 with a pawn and opens the f1-bishop's diagonal.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3.cue: Support your attacked d-pawn with a pawn.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3.note: White plays quietly, supporting d4 and freeing the f1-bishop.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops the other knight, guarding d4 and getting ready to castle.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3.note: White develops the other knight, adding a third attacker on d5 and preparing e4.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3.cue: Develop your queenside knight, adding pressure on the d5-pawn.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3.note: White plays quietly, protecting c4 so that ...dxc4 no longer wins a pawn, but it does shut in the c1-bishop.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3.note: White develops toward the centre and puts pressure on the d5-pawn.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3.note: White opens the f1-bishop to take back the c4-pawn.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3.cue: Open a line for the piece that can win back your pawn.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5.note: White pins the f6-knight to the queen, weakening Black's control of d5 and e4.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5.cue: Pin the knight that defends Black's centre pawn.

d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2.note: White develops the knight to d2 to support a later e4 push.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3.note: White saves the bishop and keeps it on the diagonal aimed at d5, with f7 behind it.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3.note: White develops the knight, defends the e5-pawn and prepares Bc4 to hit the d5-knight.
e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3.cue: Develop a piece that also protects your advanced e-pawn.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4.note: White claims the centre and challenges the c5-pawn. If Black takes on d4, White recaptures with the c-pawn and keeps a pawn in the middle.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4.cue: Put your second centre pawn forward and challenge Black's c-pawn.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3.note: The bishop retreats; Black has the centre pawn and will develop with gain of time.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+.note: White gives an early check to disturb Black, but it doesn't win anything; Black blocks while developing.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4.note: White takes the centre and prepares Be2 and castling.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2.note: White develops the knight to e2 (f3 is taken by the queen) and prepares to castle.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3.note: White develops and threatens Nxe5, winning a pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4.note: White wins the pawn back with the knight, which now sits in the centre.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4.note: White regains the pawn, centralises the knight and reopens the queen's guard of d4.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3.note: A sharper set-up: White develops fast and eyes d5, planning g4 to chase the f5-bishop with gain of time.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 c3.note: White calmly supports d4 so it can't be undermined easily, planning Nf3 and Be2 with a quiet space edge.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3.note: The calm Exchange: White aims the bishop at h7 and plans c3, Bf4 and Nf3 for easy development.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4.note: The Panov: White attacks d5 again and fights for the centre, accepting a possibly isolated d-pawn for active play.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4.cue: Attack Black's d5-pawn again with a pawn from the side.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5 Nf3.note: White develops the kingside knight and prepares to castle. Moves like c4 or Bc4 can later push the d5-knight around.
e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5 Nf3.cue: Develop your kingside knight and get closer to castling.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4.note: White builds a big pawn centre and opens the c1-bishop. The d4-pawn is safe because White's queen guards it.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4.cue: The queen has gone away — claim the centre with a pawn and free your bishop.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4.note: White grabs the centre with the d-pawn and opens the c1-bishop, which may later come to f4 and hit the queen again.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4.cue: The queen retreated — build your centre with a pawn and free a bishop.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3.note: White develops the bishop to support d4. Common plans are Qd2 and Bh6 to swap Black's fianchettoed bishop, or f3 to firm up e4.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3.cue: Develop your dark-squared bishop to a square where it supports your d-pawn.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5.note: White wins back the pawn. Now White threatens Bxf7+, picking up a pawn and exposing Black's king.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5.note: White captures the pawn that was attacking the c4-bishop, so the bishop is safe and White is a pawn up for the moment.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3.note: White develops with an attack on e5, which is unprotected: Nxe5 is now a threat.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 d3.note: White protects e4 from the f6-knight and opens the c1-bishop. Solid development; f4 or Nf3 can come next.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 d3.cue: Your e4-pawn is attacked — guard it with a pawn that frees your bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3.note: White guards e4 and opens the c1-bishop. Solid: White can follow with f4 or Nf3 and castle.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3.cue: Your e4-pawn is attacked — guard it with a pawn that frees your bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5.note: White ignores the knight and threatens Qxf7 mate (bishop and queen both hit f7). Black's next moves are forced to defend.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5.cue: Black's knight left f6 — bring your queen out with a mate threat on f7.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.note: White aims the bishop at f7 and gets ready to castle. It allows the trick ...Nxe4 Nxe4 d5, regaining the piece with a fork of bishop and knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4 d4.note: White blocks the bishop's line to f2, stopping the mate, and attacks the bishop at the same time.
e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4 d4.cue: Block the bishop's line to f2 with a pawn that also attacks it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O.note: White castles and lets e4 go, because d4 and Re1 will win the pawn back quickly.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O.cue: Leave the e4-pawn: get your king safe first.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4.note: White keeps the bishop and the pressure on c6 instead of trading. From a4 it can later drop back to b3, aimed at f7.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4.cue: Your bishop is attacked — keep it on the same diagonal, still pinning down the c6-knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3.note: White prepares d4 to build a big pawn centre, and the c3-pawn also takes the d4-square away from Black's pieces.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3.cue: Prepare to build a big centre: a small pawn move that supports a later d4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3.note: White guards e4 with a pawn and opens the c1-bishop. Quiet and solid — White avoids sharp lines and keeps a healthy centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3.cue: Your e4-pawn is attacked — defend it with a pawn that also frees your bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4.note: White recaptures and wins the pawn back, with a strong knight in the middle and the queen's d-file open. Now White just develops.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4.cue: Win back the pawn you gave — recapture with a piece that becomes strong in the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5.note: White wins back the pawn and now threatens Bxf7+, winning a pawn and dragging the king out.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3.note: White kicks the knight with a pawn and opens the c1-bishop, but stays a pawn down.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5.note: White develops the bishop with pressure on the c6-knight, which defends e5, and clears the way to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2.note: White attacks the e4-knight, and if it retreats, Nc6+ is a discovered check that wins Black's queen. Black's best is ...Qe7.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2.cue: Attack Black's knight in a way that sets up a discovered check on the e-file.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3.note: The knight retreats to its best square. White keeps the extra pawn for now, but Black is about to win it back on e4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3.cue: Your knight is attacked: send it back to its most natural square.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7.note: A tempting sacrifice: the knight hits Black's queen and rook. White gets two pawns and an exposed king for the piece, which is not enough.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2.note: White develops modestly and prepares to castle, but does nothing to stop Black taking the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5.note: White develops and pins the f6-knight to the queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3.note: White develops with an attack on the e4-knight, which has no defender yet, and clears the way to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O.note: White castles, getting the king safe and the rook ready for the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Nxe5.note: White takes a second pawn on e5. The knight is strong in the centre and eyes f7.
e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Nxe5.cue: Black left a pawn unprotected — capture it.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3.note: White develops with tempo by attacking the queen. Every queen move gives White another free developing move.
e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3.cue: Develop a piece that attacks Black's queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4.note: White recaptures with the knight, which sits strongly in the centre. Now develop quickly: Nc3, Bc4 or Be2, and castle.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4.cue: Win back the pawn by capturing with a piece that lands in the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4.note: White develops onto the diagonal that ...f6 opened: the bishop eyes g8 and makes kingside castling hard for Black.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4.cue: Black's f-pawn move opened a diagonal toward the king — develop a piece onto it.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5.note: White captures the pawn that was attacking the c4-bishop, saving the bishop and winning a pawn for the moment.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3.note: The queen retreats but keeps the threat of mate on f7 together with the c4-bishop.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3.note: White props up e4 again, but this weakens the kingside and takes the f3-square away from the g1-knight.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5.note: White trades off Black's central pawn, but this only helps Black's knight come to the centre.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4.note: The queen escapes to a4, eyeing the c6-knight and guarding e4 along the 4th rank. It is safe there for now, though a bit offside.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4.note: White regains a pawn and the queen defends e5, but the queen in the centre can be hit by Black's knight.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3.note: White defends e4 and opens the c1-bishop to win back the f4-pawn.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3.note: White supports d4 with another pawn, so that if Black takes on d4 White can recapture with a pawn and keep the chain intact.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3.cue: Black is attacking the base of your pawn chain. Support it with a pawn.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Nc3.note: White develops the knight, supporting e4 and building a solid centre before Black can attack it.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Nc3.cue: Develop another piece, protecting your e-pawn.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7.note: Black finishes the fianchetto. The bishop guards the king and sits on the long diagonal, ready for when the f6-knight moves. Castling is next.
Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7.cue: Finish what your last pawn move prepared.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O e6.note: Black backs up d5 and opens the f8-bishop, getting ready to castle with a solid pawn centre.
Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O e6.cue: Strengthen your centre pawn and free your dark bishop at the same time.

b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3 d5 Bg2 Nf6.note: Black develops and adds a defender to d5, keeping the centre solid before castling.
b3 e5 Bb2 Nc6 g3 d5 Bg2 Nf6.cue: Defend your attacked centre pawn by developing a piece.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3 Nf6.note: Black develops and prepares to castle.
c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece so you can castle soon.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6.note: Black targets b2, which the bishop left undefended when it went to f4, and adds pressure on d4.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6.note: Black prepares ...e5 to challenge White's centre and the f4-bishop.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6.note: Black develops and targets d4, which no longer has a c- or e-pawn next to it to defend it.
d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6.cue: Develop a piece that targets White's d-pawn.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5.note: Black develops the light bishop to an active square, eyeing c2 and keeping e4 under control.
d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5.cue: Develop your light bishop actively before your e-pawn moves.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6.note: Black does the same: opens the dark bishop and holds d5 firmly.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6.cue: Free your dark bishop and strengthen your centre pawn.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6.note: Black develops and adds more pressure on d4.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7.note: Black finishes the fianchetto: the bishop guards the king and waits on the long diagonal behind the f6-knight. Castling is next.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7.cue: Finish what your last pawn move prepared.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4.note: Black takes the c4-pawn. With ...c6 already played, ...b5 could protect it, so White has to spend time getting it back.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4.cue: Now it's time to take the pawn White offered.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4.note: Black grabs the c4-pawn. With ...c6 already played, Black can try to keep it with ...b5, so White must spend time winning it back.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4.cue: Now it's time to take the pawn White offered.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6.note: Black supports d5 with both c- and e-pawns, making a very solid centre (the Semi-Slav).

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5.note: Black gets the light bishop out before ...e6 locks it in. That is the main reason for playing ...c6 instead of ...e6.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5.cue: White closed in their own bishop — get yours outside the pawn chain first.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops and defends d5 a second time.
d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6.cue: Develop a kingside piece that protects your centre pawn.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6.note: Black gives the pawn back and opens the f8-bishop, preparing ...c5 and castling.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7.note: Black breaks the pin by developing the bishop, and gets ready to castle.

d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2 b6.note: Black prepares ...Bb7, putting the light bishop on the long diagonal where it can fight for e4.
d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2 b6.cue: Prepare a fianchetto for your light-squared bishop.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3 Nf6.note: Black develops and attacks the queen, so White has to spend another move on it. This is how Black gets ahead in development.
e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3 Nf6.cue: Develop a piece and attack White's queen with it at the same time.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6.note: Black develops and adds pressure on e5, the key pawn in White's centre.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight instead of exchanging on d4, keeping the queen strong in the centre.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4.note: Black trades pawns on d4, leaving White with an isolated d-pawn that can become a target later.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nc6.note: Black develops and adds control of d4 and e5; the d5-pawn is still guarded by the queen.
e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nc6.cue: Develop a queenside piece toward the centre.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6.note: Black blocks the check with a developing move, so the check gained White nothing.
e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6.cue: Block the check with a piece that wants to come out anyway.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4 e6.note: Black firms up d5 and frees the dark bishop. Black's light bishop is already outside the chain, so ...e6 locks nothing in.
e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4 e6.cue: Your light bishop is out — free the other one.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2 Be7.note: Black develops the bishop and prepares to castle. Nothing is attacked yet, so safety first.
e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2 Be7.cue: Develop your dark-squared bishop to a safe square and get ready to castle.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3 Bd6.note: Black guards e5 with a developing move and gets ready to castle.
e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3 Bd6.cue: Your e5-pawn is attacked — defend it while developing.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.note: The Classical: Black develops the bishop with tempo, threatening Bxe4 to win the undefended knight.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.cue: Develop your light bishop with an attack on the centralised knight.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.note: The Classical: Black develops the bishop with tempo, threatening Bxe4 to win the undefended knight.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5.cue: Develop your light bishop with an attack on the centralised knight.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6.note: Black finishes the pawn chain and frees the dark bishop; the f5-bishop is ready to drop back to g6 if hit.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6.cue: Open the way for your dark-squared bishop.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 c3 e6.note: Black completes the solid pawn chain and frees the dark bishop. Next comes ...c5 to attack White's d4 base.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 c3 e6.cue: Your light bishop is out — now open the way for the other bishop.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6.note: Black develops and puts pressure on the d4-pawn straight away, so White has to spend a move defending it.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6.cue: Develop a piece that pressures the d4-pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6.note: Black defends d5 with a piece while developing; the knight also guards the kingside.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6.cue: Defend the attacked d5-pawn by developing a piece.

e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Nxd5 Nf3 g6.note: Black prepares to put the bishop on g7, where it will press against White's d4-pawn from long range, and then castle.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to a natural square and prepares to castle kingside, keeping an eye on e4 and d5.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6.note: Black develops the knight to its natural square and prepares to castle kingside.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 c6.note: Black prepares queenside counterplay with ...b5 or ...Qa5, and controls d5 and b5.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5.note: Black blocks the bishop's line to f7 and attacks it at the same time, gaining a tempo while taking the centre.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5.cue: Your f7-pawn is in danger: block the bishop's diagonal with a pawn that also attacks it.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5 c6.note: Black offers a pawn to open lines: if dxc6, ...Nxc6 gives Black quick development, and otherwise ...cxd5 wins the pawn back.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5 c6.cue: Undermine White's advanced d-pawn with a pawn from the side.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6.note: Black protects e5 with a pawn and opens the c8-bishop. Solid and simple.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6.cue: Your e-pawn is attacked: support it with a pawn that frees your other bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 Nc6.note: Black develops naturally and guards e5. Both sides finish developing; watch for ...Na5 hitting the c4-bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3 Bb4.note: Black develops with a pin on the c3-knight, which guards e4. Black may follow with ...d5 or ...Bxc3 to weaken White's pawns.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6.note: Black's knight guards f7 and stops the mate, and it also attacks the c4-bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.note: Black develops the bishop to its most active diagonal, aiming at f2, and prepares to castle.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5.cue: Mirror White: put your kingside bishop on its most active diagonal.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4 d4 Qxe4+.note: Black takes the e4-pawn with check, attacking the e5-knight too. But the c5-bishop is still attacked by the d4-pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4.note: Black takes the pawn. White will regain it, but Black heads for a simplified, very solid position.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6.note: Black develops and hits e4. White doesn't need to defend it directly, because castling sets up Re1 and tactics on the e-file.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6.note: Black develops and hits e4, which c3 has left without a defender — ...Nxe4 is a real threat.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6.note: Black supports e5 with a pawn and opens the light-squared bishop, but doesn't yet hit e4, so White can push d4 at once.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5.note: Black develops the bishop actively toward f2 and gets ready to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5.note: Black develops with a threat: the d4-knight is hit by the bishop and the c6-knight, but defended only by the queen, so ...Bxd4 would win it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6.note: Black develops and hits e4, which is no longer guarded. A sound alternative to ...Bc5: Black aims for quick development and pressure on White's centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4.note: An aggressive queen sortie: Black attacks the unguarded e4-pawn (...Qxe4+) and eyes f2/h2. It wins a pawn if White is careless but leaves the queen exposed.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5.note: Black blocks the bishop's path to f7 and attacks the bishop at the same time.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5.cue: Your f7-pawn is in danger: block the bishop's diagonal with a pawn that also attacks it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6.note: The knight returns to safety, keeping the extra pawn and guarding the kingside.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6.cue: Your knight is attacked: bring it back to a safe square near your king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4.note: Black mirrors White: develop the bishop with the same pressure on the c3-knight, which guards e4, and prepare to castle.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4.cue: Copy your opponent's idea: develop your kingside bishop to pressure a knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6.note: Black counterattacks the e5-knight instead of saving the e4-knight. It fails: White takes on e4 and the e-file tactics still work.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4.note: Now that White's knight has left e5, Black safely regains the pawn: material is level and the knight sits actively in the centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4.cue: Material is down a pawn: win it back now that the knight has gone.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7.note: Black simply takes the knight. The king looks exposed, but Black is a piece for two pawns up and can tuck the king away (e.g. ...Kg8) later.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7.cue: A knight has jumped in and forks two pieces: can you just remove it?

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5.note: Black grabs the centre with a pawn and threatens ...dxe4, since that pawn would win e4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5.cue: White is passive: strike in the centre with a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7.note: Black breaks the pin by putting the bishop between knight and queen, and gets ready to castle.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7.cue: Your knight is pinned to the queen: develop a piece that breaks the pin.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5.note: Black guards the knight with a pawn and claims the centre. It also leaves ...exd4 as a threat, since the bishop on d3 blocks the queen from defending d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5.cue: Your knight is attacked: defend it with a pawn that also grabs the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Ne7.note: Black develops the knight to e7, since f6 is taken by the queen, and prepares to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Nxe5 Qxd5.note: Black wins back a pawn and attacks the e5-knight, which has no defender — ...Qxe5+ is threatened.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd7.note: The queen steps back but blocks the c8-bishop and stands on the same diagonal as Black's king — a costly mistake.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7.note: An odd queen move: Black eyes the e4-pawn (hoping for ...Qxe4+) but blocks the f8-bishop, so Black's development gets stuck.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6.note: Black develops the queen's knight and adds another defender to e5.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 e4.note: Black pushes the e-pawn to kick the queen. Black gains time and space, and the d5-pawn can be won back later.
e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 e4.cue: White's queen stands where one of your pawns can attack it.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6.note: Black develops and blocks the f-file, ending the mate threat on f7. The knight also eyes e4.
e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6.cue: Mate on f7 is threatened again: develop a piece that blocks the queen's line.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3 d5.note: Black strikes in the centre with a pawn while White's pieces are undeveloped and the kingside is loosened.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3 d5.cue: White wasted time with a pawn move: grab the centre with a pawn.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5 Nxd5.note: Black recaptures with a piece, keeping the material level and placing the knight on a strong central square.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5 Nxd5.cue: A pawn was just taken: win it back with a piece.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4 Nf6.note: Black develops another piece with pressure on e4.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4 Nf6.cue: Keep developing: bring out a kingside piece that pressures White's e-pawn.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4 Nc6.note: Black develops with tempo, attacking the queen.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4 Nc6.cue: White's queen sits in the centre: develop a piece that attacks it.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6.note: Black keeps developing. The f4-pawn will probably fall, but Black will be well developed.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6.cue: Keep developing: bring out your other knight.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6.note: Black develops and adds pressure on d4, the key square in White's centre.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Qb6.note: Black's queen attacks d4 and b2 at once, before developing the knights.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops and attacks e4, which is well defended by the c3-knight. Black is ready to castle kingside.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3.note: White develops the bishop toward Black's kingside and clears the way to castle.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O e6 d4.note: White finally challenges the centre and hits c5, hoping to open lines for the g2-bishop.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3 Nf6 Be2.note: White develops quietly and gets ready to castle.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3.note: White develops and lets Black take b2. After ...Qxb2?, Nb5 threatens Nc7+ and Rb1, and Black gets into big trouble.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 Qb6 Nc3.cue: Ignore the attack on b2 — develop a piece that punishes the pawn grab.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6 Be2.note: White develops simply and gets ready to castle, keeping the solid London setup.
d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6 Be2.cue: Develop your last kingside piece so you can castle.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Ne5.note: White jumps forward to trade off Black's c6-knight and eyes f7.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3.note: White completes the c3-d4-e3 triangle so d4 is secure, and opens a diagonal for the queen toward b3.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2.note: White develops the knight to d2, where it doesn't block the c-pawn. That way c3 can be played to hold d4.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2.cue: Develop your other knight without blocking your c-pawn.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3.note: White develops the bishop toward Black's king and gets ready to castle.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4.note: White stops ...b5, which would protect the extra pawn, so the c4-pawn can be won back with e3 and Bxc4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4.note: White stops ...b5, which would protect the extra c4-pawn, so the pawn can be won back with e3 and Bxc4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3.note: White guards c4 and opens the f1-bishop, keeping a solid centre.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3.cue: Protect your c-pawn and open a path for your kingside bishop.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5.note: White exchanges pawns to open the c-file and the f1-bishop's diagonal, getting ready for Qb3 to hit b7 now that Black's bishop has left c8.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops the other knight, guarding d4 and getting ready to castle.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4.note: White regains the pawn with the bishop and gets ready to castle.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4.cue: Win back your pawn while developing a piece.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3.note: White guards c4 and opens the f1-bishop, building a solid centre.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3.cue: Protect your c-pawn and open a path for your other bishop.

d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2 b6 Bb5+.note: White develops with check, aiming to disturb Black's development; the bishop is easily pushed back, though.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3 Nf6 Qf3.note: The queen retreats to safety, where it eyes f6 and lines up with the b3-bishop against d5.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.note: White develops with tempo, hitting the undefended d5-knight and preparing to castle kingside.
e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4.cue: Develop a bishop with tempo by attacking the centralized knight.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops the kingside knight, supporting d4 and preparing Be2 and castling.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 Nf3.cue: Develop your kingside knight, supporting your d-pawn.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4.note: White recaptures with the pawn, keeping a central pawn on d4 and opening the c3-square for the knight.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4.cue: Win back the pawn while keeping a pawn in the centre.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nc6 Qf3.note: An early queen move: it adds a second attacker on d5 (with the b3-bishop) and threatens Qxd5.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6 Bxc6+.note: White gives up the bishop for the knight with check; Black gets the bishop pair and an extra central pawn on c6.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4 e6 Be2.note: White breaks the pin by developing and prepares to castle.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2 Be7 exd5.note: White trades on d5, opening the bishop's diagonal toward h7 and threatening dxc6.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3 Bd6 d4.note: White pushes d4 a move later, threatening dxe5. But this leaves e4 loose, and Black can hit the f3-knight.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3.note: White saves the knight and hits the bishop back, gaining a tempo.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3.note: White saves the knight and hits the bishop back, gaining a tempo.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4.note: An aggressive lunge: White threatens gxf5, winning the bishop, and gains kingside space with tempo.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 c3 e6 Be2.note: White develops modestly and prepares Nf3 and castling. Black answers with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6 pressure on d4.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3.note: White props up d4 with a pawn, building a solid chain. Black keeps developing with ...Nf6 and ...Bg4.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3.note: White adds a third attacker on d5 and develops, keeping up the pressure.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3.cue: Add another attacker on d5 while developing.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops the kingside knight, guards d4 and gets ready to castle. Simple development is the plan because Black has spent moves with the queen.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3.cue: Develop your kingside knight to its best square, supporting your d-pawn.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6 Nf3.note: White develops the kingside knight, supports d4 and prepares to castle. White is ahead in development thanks to chasing the queen.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6 Nf3.cue: Develop your kingside knight to its natural square.

e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 c6 Nf3.note: White develops the kingside knight, strengthening d4 and preparing to castle.
e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 c6 Nf3.cue: Develop your last minor kingside piece and get ready to castle.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3.note: The bishop retreats and hits the e4-knight, but it is a mistake: it lets Black use the e-file against White's knight and king.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5 c6 Nc3.note: White develops and adds a defender to d5, but leaves the queen on f3 where Black's e-pawn can hit it.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6 O-O.note: White castles and will continue with d3 or d4 in the centre.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3 Bb4 Ne2.note: White develops so that ...Bxc3+ can be met by Nxc3, keeping a healthy pawn structure. The f-pawn also stays free to advance.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nc6 d3 Bb4 Ne2.cue: Develop your other knight to a square that would let it recapture on c3.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3.note: White keeps the bishop on the diagonal to f7, so the pressure on f7 stays.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3.cue: Your bishop is attacked — move it but keep it aimed at f7.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3.note: White guards e4 solidly and frees the c1-bishop. A slow, Italian-style game follows.

e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4 d4 Qxe4+ Be3.note: White blocks the check while developing; d4 guards the knight and still attacks the c5-bishop. White's lead in development grows and Black's queen will be chased.
e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4 d4 Qxe4+ Be3.cue: Block the check with a piece that develops.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.note: White hits e5 and opens the centre. Black's king is still in the middle, so open lines favour White.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.cue: Open the centre with a pawn move that attacks e5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O.note: White castles instead of guarding e4: if Black grabs the pawn, Re1 and d4 win it back with a lead in development.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O.cue: Don't worry about e4 yet — get your king safe and your rook toward the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3.note: White calmly guards e4 with a pawn and opens the c1-bishop. This is the slow 'quiet Italian': solid centre first, action later.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3.cue: Your e4-pawn is attacked — guard it with a pawn and free your dark-squared bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4.note: White pushes d4 straight away, grabbing the centre and attacking the c5-bishop (threatening dxc5). Black must take or retreat.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4.cue: Black didn't challenge e4 — grab the centre with a pawn that also hits Black's bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O.note: White castles, putting the king safe before the centre opens. Next come c3 and Re1 with a slow build-up.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O.cue: Your king is still in the middle — get it to safety.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3.note: White defends the knight with a developing move, and the bishop now hits c5 too: Nxc6 followed by Bxc5 is threatened, so Black must stay alert.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3.cue: Your d4-knight is attacked twice — defend it with a piece that also develops and eyes Black's bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6.note: White trades on c6 first so Black must recapture (the knight attacks the queen). This damages Black's pawns and clears the way for e5 to kick the f6-knight.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6.cue: Trade first: capture the c6-knight, which also hits Black's queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5.note: White ignores e4 and counterattacks: the knight threatens Nxc7+, forking the king and the a8-rook. Black has to deal with that first.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5.cue: Counterattack instead of defending: your knight can threaten a royal fork on c7.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3.note: The bishop retreats and attacks the e4-knight, but it is a mistake: it lets Black use the e-file against White's knight and king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5.note: White goes after f7: Nxf7 would fork the queen and rook. But moving the same piece again costs time while White is already a pawn down.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O.note: White castles before anything else. The e5-pawn is not yet worth taking, so safety comes first.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6 Qxe4.note: White takes the knight and threatens Nc6+, a discovered check that also attacks Black's queen. Black must stop it at once.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6 Qxe4.cue: Grab the hanging knight — your queen will line up on Black's king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d3.note: White kicks the e4-knight with a pawn, so it must retreat. Simple and safe: White keeps a small lead in development.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d3.cue: Kick Black's knight out of the centre with a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4.note: White builds a big centre and opens the c1-bishop. The plan is Bd3, castling and Re1 to put pressure on Black's e4-knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5.note: White trades in the centre and the d5-pawn now attacks the c6-knight, so Black must recapture.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3.note: White develops another knight and supports d5 and e4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5.note: White wins back the pawn before Black can take on d4. The knight on e5 is strong and eyes f7.

e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Ne7 Nc3.note: White develops and eyes d5, where the knight would hit Black's queen and the c7-pawn. d4 is coming too.
e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Ne7 Nc3.cue: Develop a knight toward the centre — it eyes a square that hits Black's queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Nxe5 Qxd5 Qe2.note: White defends the knight with the queen and lines up on the e-file against Black's king. White stays a clean pawn up.
e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Nf6 Nxe5 Qxd5 Qe2.cue: Your e5-knight is undefended — protect it while lining up on Black's king.

e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd7 Bb5.note: White pins the queen to the king, threatening Bxd7+. Black must block the pin (...c6 is best), and White keeps a big lead in development.
e4 e5 Nf3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd7 Bb5.cue: Black's queen and king share a diagonal — pin the queen with a developing move.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7 Nc3.note: White guards e4 with a developing move, so Black's queen achieves nothing. White is clearly ahead in development.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7 Nc3.cue: Black's queen is eyeing your e4-pawn — guard it while developing a piece.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6 h3.note: White stops ...Bg4, which would pin the f3-knight — the knight that helps hold d4. Now White can develop calmly.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6 h3.cue: Stop Black's bishop from pinning your f3-knight with a small pawn move.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 e4 Qd1.note: The queen goes all the way home. White has wasted time, and Black's pawn on e4 cramps White's kingside pieces.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6 c3.note: White prepares d4 but still hasn't developed the kingside knight; the queen on f3 even takes its best square.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3 d5 Nc3.note: White develops and adds pressure on d5.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 c4.note: White chases the knight with a pawn. It gains a tempo, but it leaves d3 weak and the d4-square permanently without pawn cover.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4 Nf6 Nc3.note: White defends e4 with the knight and develops.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4 Nc6 Bb5.note: White pins the c6-knight to the king, so it cannot take the queen for now.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bxf4.note: White regains the pawn, so material is level again.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3.note: White develops and adds another defender to d4 and e5.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3.cue: Develop a piece that protects both your d-pawn and your e-pawn.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Qb6 Nf3.note: White develops and adds a defender to d4 and e5. Black's pressure on d4 is now met.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Qb6 Nf3.cue: Develop a piece that protects your d-pawn and e-pawn.

e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Nc3 Nf6 Be3.note: White develops the dark-squared bishop, protecting d4. A typical plan is Qd2 and Bh6 to trade off Black's strong g7-bishop.
e4 g6 d4 Bg7 Nf3 d6 Nc3 Nf6 Be3.cue: Develop your dark-squared bishop to a safe square where it supports your centre.

Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O.note: Black puts the king safe behind the fianchetto. Next come ...c5 or ...Nc6 to fight for the centre.
Nf3 d5 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O.cue: Your kingside is ready — make your king safe.

Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O e6 d4 Nc6.note: Black develops and adds pressure on d4. If dxc5, Black recaptures with the bishop and is comfortable.
Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nf6 O-O e6 d4 Nc6.cue: Develop your queenside knight to add pressure on White's d-pawn.

c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3 Nf6 Be2 c5.note: Black takes space and controls d4, keeping White's pieces out of the centre and making a secure spot for the b4-bishop. Black stays a pawn up and comfortable.
c4 e5 b4 Bxb4 Bb2 d6 e3 Nf6 Be2 c5.cue: Take space with a pawn that controls d4 and backs up your advanced bishop.

d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e3 d6 Be2 O-O.note: Black puts the king safe behind the fianchetto before starting central play with ...e5 or ...c5.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4.note: Black develops and pins the f3-knight to the queen, weakening one of d4's defenders.
d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4.cue: Develop your light bishop and pin the knight that guards d4.

d4 d5 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 Ne5 Nxe5.note: Black simply trades knights. After dxe5 the f6-knight moves (e.g. to e4) and Black stands well, with White's centre pawn pulled to e5.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3 Nc6.note: Black develops and puts more pressure on d4.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3 Nc6.cue: Develop your queenside knight to press on d4.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 e6.note: Black backs up c5 and opens the f8-bishop, building a solid centre.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O.note: Black puts the king safe behind the fianchetto, ready to fight for the centre with ...c5 or ...Nc6.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O.cue: Your kingside is ready — make your king safe.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5.note: Black brings the light bishop out before playing ...e6, and the bishop also makes e4 harder for White.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5.cue: Get your light bishop outside the pawn chain before you close it in.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5.note: Black brings the light bishop out before playing ...e6, so it won't be shut in behind the pawns. It also keeps White from playing e4 easily.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5.cue: Get your light bishop outside the pawn chain before you close it in.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7.note: Black develops, supporting a later ...e5 or ...c5 break.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures with the c-pawn, keeping a pawn on d5 and getting a symmetrical, solid centre.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5.cue: Win back the pawn and keep a pawn in the centre.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.note: Black develops the queenside knight to its best square, pressing on d4 and controlling e5 and b4.
d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6.cue: Develop your queenside knight to its most natural square, eyeing d4.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5.note: Black hits d4, Black's main way to fight for the centre in this line.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O.note: Black puts the king safe before thinking about ...dxc4 or ...b6.

d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2 b6 Bb5+ c6.note: Black blocks the check with a pawn that attacks the bishop, so White must spend another move retreating.
d4 d5 e3 e6 Nf3 Nf6 Nbd2 b6 Bb5+ c6.cue: Block the check with a pawn that also attacks the checking piece.

e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3 Nf6 Qf3 a5.note: Black goes after the b3-bishop: ...a4 next would leave it nowhere safe to go, so White has to deal with this right away.
e3 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 d5 Bb3 Nf6 Qf3 a5.cue: White's bishop on b3 has few safe squares — start a pawn march to trap it.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6.note: Black saves the knight and attacks the c4-bishop at the same time, forcing White to move it again.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bg4.note: Black develops the bishop and puts pressure on the f3-knight, which supports d4. A common follow-up is ...e6 and ...Nc6.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6.note: Black develops with pressure on d4: knight and queen both attack it and only White's queen defends, so Black threatens to win the pawn.

e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nc6 Qf3 Nf6.note: Black defends d5 with a developing move. Next ...Bg4 or ...e6 hits the queen or solidifies, and White's queen has wasted time.
e4 c6 Bc4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb3 Nc6 Qf3 Nf6.cue: Your d5-pawn is attacked twice — defend it while developing.

e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6 Bxc6+ bx.note: Black recaptures toward the centre, so the c6 and d5 pawns form a strong duo, and the two bishops give Black the easier game.
