e4 c6 Nc3 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bb5+ Nc6 Bxc6+ bx.cue: You're in check — recapture so your pawns point toward the centre.

e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4 e6 Be2 Nd7.note: Black develops flexibly, preparing ...Ngf6 and keeping ...dxe4 in reserve; the knight on d7 guards e5 and f6.
e4 c6 Nf3 d5 Nc3 Bg4 d4 e6 Be2 Nd7.cue: Develop your queenside knight to a modest square that supports your kingside knight.

e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2 Be7 exd5 cxd5.note: Black recaptures and is left with two big centre pawns on d5 and e5, the better side of the position.
e4 c6 Qf3 d5 Bd3 e5 Ne2 Be7 exd5 cxd5.cue: Recapture so you keep two pawns in the centre.

e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3 Bd6 d4 dxe4.note: Black grabs e4 and attacks the f3-knight, threatening exf3. White usually answers Nxe5, and Black develops easily with ...Nf6.
e4 c6 d3 d5 Bd2 e5 Nf3 Bd6 d4 dxe4.cue: Capture a central pawn and hit a white knight at the same time.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6.note: The bishop retreats but stays on its good diagonal, aiming at White's queenside and c2.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6.cue: Your bishop is attacked — retreat it without leaving its diagonal.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6.note: The bishop retreats but stays on its good diagonal, aiming at White's queenside and c2.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6.cue: Your bishop is attacked — retreat it without leaving its diagonal.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6.note: The bishop must move; it retreats but stays on the useful b1-h7 diagonal. White's g4 push has also loosened White's kingside.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6.cue: Your bishop is attacked by a pawn — retreat it but keep it on its diagonal.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6.note: Black develops toward the centre and guards the kingside (h7). Next ...Bg4 or ...g6 brings the last minor pieces out.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6.cue: Bring out a kingside piece that also helps guard h7.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6.note: Black adds a pawn defender to d5 and frees the f8-bishop, aiming to castle quickly.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6.cue: Support d5 with a pawn and free your dark-squared bishop.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bf5.note: Black brings the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before playing ...e6, and eyes the c2-pawn.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6 d4 Nf6 Nf3 a6.note: A prophylactic pawn move: it takes b5 away from White's knight and bishop, so Nb5 can't harass the queen and Bb5+ is not possible.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7.note: Black attacks the unprotected e5-knight. It can't simply retreat (e.g. Nf3?? Nc3+, discovered check winning the queen), so Black wins material.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7.cue: Use the e-file: line up your queen against the undefended knight and White's king.

e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5 c6 Nc3 e4.note: Black kicks the queen with a pawn, gaining time. After the queen moves, ...cxd5 wins back the pawn with a good centre.
e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 Qf3 d5 exd5 c6 Nc3 e4.cue: White's queen stands on a square one of your pawns can attack.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6 O-O O-O.note: Black castles too. Development is complete and the position is equal.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3 d6 O-O O-O.cue: Your king is still in the centre: get it safe.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6.note: Black guards e5, which the queen was attacking (Qxe5+ would win a pawn with check).

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 O-O.note: Black gets the king safe. Everything is developed; next ideas are ...d6 and ...h6 or ...a6.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 O-O.cue: You are developed: get your king safe.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6.note: Black retreats with a threat: the knight attacks the b5-bishop, and it also keeps watch on f5 and c4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7.note: Black develops quietly and prepares to castle. This is the main 'Closed' Ruy Lopez.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4.note: Black grabs the e4-pawn — the Open Ruy Lopez. It's playable because White's quick d4 and Re1 regain the pawn, so this leads to open, active play rather than a pawn up.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6.note: Black also supports the centre with a pawn and opens the c8-bishop, which may go to g4 or e6.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4.note: Black takes, removing the pawn that attacked the bishop. White will recapture and keep a big pawn centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6.note: Black supports e5 with a pawn and opens the c8-bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6.note: Black piles up on d4: bishop, knight and now queen all attack it, so ...Bxd4 would win the knight. The queen also eyes f2.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6.note: Black recaptures toward the centre with the b-pawn: this keeps the d-file closed (no early queen trade) and supports a later ...d5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4.note: Black develops with check, gaining time and keeping the plan of ...Qxe4+ alive.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7.note: Black attacks the unprotected e5-knight. It can't simply retreat (e.g. Nf3?? Nc3+, discovered check winning the queen), so Black wins material.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7.cue: Use the e-file: line up your queen against the undefended knight and White's king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5 d5.note: Black blocks the bishop's line to f7 with a pawn that also attacks the bishop, ending the threat with tempo.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5 d5.cue: f7 is under fire: block the bishop's diagonal with a pawn that also attacks it.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O.note: Black castles too. The position stays symmetrical and very solid.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O.cue: Your king is still in the centre: get it safe.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6 Qxe4 Bxe.note: Black removes the dangerous knight, but the bishop on e5 is now attacked by White's queen and has no defender.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d3 Nf6.note: The knight retreats to its natural square, where it helps guard Black's king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5.note: Black stakes out the centre too, and the d5-pawn props up the knight on e4 so it cannot be chased off easily.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5.cue: Support your centralised knight with a pawn that also claims the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5 Nxd5.note: Black recaptures with the knight, which now sits in the centre, and the material is level.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5 Nxd5.cue: Recapture in the centre so material is level and your c6-knight is no longer attacked.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3 h6.note: Black asks the bishop a question: retreat or trade itself for the knight.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3 h6.cue: Ask White's pinning bishop to decide: attack it with a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Bd6.note: Black develops by challenging the strong e5-knight and gets ready to castle. Both sides have centralised knights.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Bd6.cue: Develop your kingside bishop to a square that challenges White's centralised knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7 Nc3 Nf6.note: Black develops and puts more pressure on e4.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6 h3 Nge7.note: Black develops the kingside knight via e7, since the f6-pawn blocks its normal square.

e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 e4 Qd1 Bc5.note: Black develops to an active diagonal aimed at f2 and prepares to castle, enjoying a clear lead in development.
e4 e5 Qf3 Nf6 Bc4 d5 exd5 e4 Qd1 Bc5.cue: Develop your kingside bishop to the diagonal aimed at White's f2.

e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6 c3 Na5.note: The knight attacks the c4-bishop, White's most dangerous attacker of f7. Black is happy to trade knight for bishop and get the bishop pair.
e4 e5 Qh5 Nc6 Bc4 g6 Qf3 Nf6 c3 Na5.cue: White's most dangerous bishop is loose: chase it with a knight.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3 d5 Nc3 d4.note: Black pushes on with tempo: the pawn attacks the c3-knight, which must move again, and Black gains lots of space.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Bg5 Nc6 f3 d5 Nc3 d4.cue: Push a centre pawn forward to attack a knight and gain space.

e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 c4 Nf6.note: The knight steps back to a safe, useful square. With the d-file open, Black's queen now eyes the weak d3-pawn, and ...Bxh3 is still in the air.
e4 e5 d3 Nf6 Nh3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 c4 Nf6.cue: Your knight is attacked by a pawn: retreat it to a good, safe square.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4.note: Black pins the c3-knight to the king and also blocks the queen's guard of e4 along the 4th rank, so ...Nxe4 is now a threat.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6 Qa4 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4.cue: Pin the knight that guards White's e-pawn, cutting off the queen's defence at the same time.

e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4 Nc6 Bb5 Bd7.note: Black breaks the pin by developing. Now the knight really threatens ...Nxd4, winning the queen, so White must deal with it.
e4 e5 d4 exd4 e5 d6 Qxd4 Nc6 Bb5 Bd7.cue: Your knight is pinned: develop a piece that blocks the pin, renewing the threat to the queen.

e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bxf4 d5.note: Black strikes in the centre, opening lines while White's king is exposed by the missing f-pawn.
e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bxf4 d5.cue: Material is level: grab the centre with a pawn.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Bd7.note: Black develops the light-squared bishop quietly, keeping options like ...Qb6 and ...Rc8 to build more pressure on the c-file and d4.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6.note: Black adds a third attacker on d4 and also eyes b2, which ties down White's c1-bishop.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Qb6 Nf3 Bd7.note: Black develops the bishop and plans ...Bb5 to swap off its light-squared bishop, which is often hemmed in by Black's own pawns.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Nb.note: White develops the other knight; from d2 it can break the pin by recapturing on f3 if needed.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3 Nc6 Bd3.note: White offers to swap light bishops; Black's f5-bishop is one of Black's best pieces.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 e6 c3.note: White completes the London pawn triangle (c3-d4-e3), which keeps d4 rock-solid against Black's pressure.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 c5 e3 Nc6 Nbd2 e6 c3.cue: Complete your pawn triangle so your d-pawn is secure.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O O-O.note: White castles too, and both kings are safe.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3.note: White opens the f1-bishop's diagonal so it can take back on c4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3.note: White opens the f1-bishop's diagonal so it can recapture the c4-pawn next move.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3.note: White develops the bishop toward Black's kingside and gets ready to castle.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3.cue: Develop your kingside bishop toward Black's king so you can castle.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5 Qb3.note: White attacks b7, which lost its guard when the bishop left c8, and also adds pressure on d5.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bf.note: White develops the dark bishop outside the pawn chain before playing e3.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O.note: White gets the king safe before deciding what to do about the tension on d4.
d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O.cue: Get your king to safety before the centre opens.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3.note: White develops the last knight, guarding d4 and getting ready to castle.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3.cue: Develop your last knight so you can castle.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb3.note: White retreats the bishop to safety on b3, where it still eyes the f7-pawn along the diagonal.
e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb3.cue: Your bishop is attacked. Retreat it to a square where it stays on the same diagonal.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6 N.note: White develops and adds a second defender to d4, stopping Black from winning the pawn.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6 N.cue: Your d-pawn is attacked twice. Develop a piece that also defends it.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: White threatens h5, which would trap the g6-bishop since h7 is blocked by Black's own pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: White threatens h5, which would trap the g6-bishop since h7 is blocked by Black's own pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2.note: White develops the knight to e2, aiming for Nf4 or h4-h5 to hunt the g6-bishop.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4.note: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before playing Nf3. Black usually answers ...Bg4, pinning or harassing.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3.note: White develops and guards d4, preparing to castle; Black now chooses where to put the dark bishop.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3.cue: Develop your kingside knight and prepare to castle.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bf5 N.note: White's knight jumps to a strong central square, eyeing f7. The plan is Bc4 and sometimes g4 to chase the f5-bishop and gain space.
e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bf5 N.cue: Put your knight on an active central post that eyes f7.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 N.note: White attacks the d6-knight, the only guard of f7: Nxd6+ cxd6 Qxf7 would be mate.
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 N.cue: Attack the knight that is guarding f7 — remove the defender and mate follows.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bx.note: White trades bishop for knight, doubling Black's pawns and removing the defender of e5. White will then take on e5 with tempo.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bx.cue: Your bishop is attacked — give it up for the knight that guards e5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.note: White now guards e4 with the rook. That also sets up a real threat: Bxc6 and Nxe5, since e4 is safe.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.cue: Your e4-pawn needs protection now — use a piece that wasn't in play yet.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.note: White hits e5 at once and opens lines toward Black's king, which is still in the centre. The pawn will be regained.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.cue: Hit back in the centre with a pawn, opening lines while Black's king is uncastled.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O.note: White castles: the king is safe, and the rook can come to e1 to support the centre and a later d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O.cue: Your pieces are out — get your king to safety.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4.note: White recaptures with the c-pawn, building a classic e4+d4 centre and attacking the bishop once more.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4.cue: Recapture so that you get two pawns side by side in the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6 c3.note: White prepares d4 and gives the bishop a retreat on c2 later. It also keeps Black's knight off d4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6 c3.cue: Prepare a later d4 with a small pawn move that also controls d4.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c.note: White adds a pawn guard to the d4-knight, so it is defended three times and can't be won. A solid pawn defender is better than moving the knight.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c.cue: Your d4-knight is attacked three times — give it one more defender, ideally a pawn.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6.note: White pushes with tempo: the f6-knight is attacked and must move. White gains space and the knight usually goes to d5, where c4 can chase it again.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nxc6 bxc6.cue: Push a centre pawn forward to chase away Black's f6-knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4 B.note: White blocks the check with a developing move that also attacks the b4-bishop. The Nxc7+ fork is still threatened.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4 B.cue: Block the check with a piece that develops and attacks the checking bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7 B.note: White takes the knight, hoping to rescue the material, but the bishop on e4 is about to be pinned.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5 d5 Bb5.note: The bishop escapes with check, but it will be hit again by ...c6, costing White more time.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O d3.note: White firmly defends e4 and opens the c1-bishop, which often goes to g5 to pin the f6-knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6 Qxe4 Bxe.note: White takes the bishop with check, ending a whole piece up. The queen also eyes g7.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Bd6 Qxe4 Bxe.cue: Win back the piece — capture with check.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Nc.note: White develops toward the centre. Plans include d4, Bd3 or Be2, and castling — normal play with an easy position.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Nc.cue: Develop a piece toward the centre.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3.note: White develops toward the kingside and attacks the knight on e4, preparing to castle next.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-.note: White castles. Black has a free, comfortable position with a strong knight on d5 and easy development.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3 h6 Bxf6.note: White gives up the bishop for the knight rather than retreat. Black must recapture, as the bishop also hits e7 and g7.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Bd6 O-.note: White gets the king safe and brings the rook toward the centre before starting any action.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7 Nc3 Nf6 Bg.note: White develops with a pin: the f6-knight can't move without exposing the queen on e7, so ...Nxe4 is off the table. Qd2 and long castling often follow.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qe7 Nc3 Nf6 Bg.cue: Develop a bishop to pin Black's f6-knight against the queen behind it.

e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6 h3 Nge7 O-O.note: White castles and is ahead in development. Next ideas are Nc3 and pressure on the a2-g8 diagonal, where Black's king is uncomfortable.
e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 f6 Bc4 Nc6 h3 Nge7 O-O.cue: You're well developed — get your king safe.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3.note: White prepares b4 to gain space on the queenside and, by covering b4, keeps Black's pieces from landing there.
e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3.cue: Prepare to grab queenside space with a pawn push.

d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Nb.note: Black opens the f8-bishop, planning ...Bd6 to trade off White's strong London bishop, and gets ready to castle.
d4 d5 Bf4 c5 e3 cxd4 exd4 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 Nb.cue: Open a diagonal for your dark bishop so it can challenge White's active bishop.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3 Nc6 Bd3 N.note: Black puts the knight on a strong central square. If White plays Bxe4, then ...dxe4 attacks the f3-knight and gains time.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Bf4 Bf5 e3 e6 c3 Nc6 Bd3 N.cue: Jump a knight into the strong central square in front of your pawns.

d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O O-O.note: Black develops the last minor piece, putting more pressure on d4. Ideas like ...Nb4 to swap off the d3-bishop can follow.
d4 d5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6 e3 Bg7 Bd3 O-O O-O.cue: Develop your last minor piece so it adds pressure on d4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.note: Black gives up the c4-pawn and opens the f8-bishop instead, aiming to develop quickly and castle.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.cue: Open the diagonal for your dark-squared bishop with a small pawn move.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.note: Black accepts that the c4-pawn will be lost and opens a diagonal for the f8-bishop instead, aiming for quick development and castling.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.cue: Open the diagonal for your dark-squared bishop with a small pawn move.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 d.note: Black takes on c4 with gain of time, since the d3-bishop has to recapture and use a second move.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5 Qb3.note: Black guards b7 and hits back down the open c-file: the c1-bishop is unprotected, so Black threatens ...Qxc1+.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5 cxd5 cxd5 Qb3.cue: Protect the b7-pawn with a piece that also attacks something of White's down an open file.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bf.note: Black copies White and develops the light bishop outside the pawns before ...e6 closes it in.
d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bf.cue: Get your light bishop out before you play a pawn move that would lock it in.

d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O.note: Black prepares ...b5 to chase the c4-bishop and gain queenside space, with ...Bb7 to follow.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h.note: Black asks the g5-bishop what it wants: retreat or trade for the knight. Black also gives the king a safe square (luft).

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb3.note: Black gains space and kicks the bishop again, threatening to win it. The c4-pawn also takes the d3-square away from White's pieces.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6 N.note: Black targets the knight that defends d4. The idea is ...Bxf3, damaging White's pawns or removing a defender, and then ...Qxd4.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: Black makes an escape square on h7, so after h5 the bishop can drop back safely. Without this, h5 would trap the bishop.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.cue: White threatens to trap your bishop with a pawn push — give it an escape square.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: Black makes an escape square on h7, so after h5 the bishop can drop back safely. Without this, h5 would trap the bishop.
e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.cue: White threatens to trap your bishop with a pawn push — give it an escape square.

e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5.note: Black strikes back at d4, the base of White's pawn chain, before White's kingside attack gets going. Typical follow-up: ...Nc6.
e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5.cue: Hit the base of White's pawn chain with a pawn.

e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3.note: Black pins the c3-knight, a key defender of d5 and e4, and gets ready to castle.
e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Nf3.cue: Develop your dark bishop actively: pin a knight that guards d5.

e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5 d4 Nf6 Nf3 Bf5 N.note: A solid move: it covers d5 and b5, giving the queen a retreat to c7 or d8. Black wants to finish with ...e6 and ...Nbd7.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 N.note: Black hits the queen with a pawn to gain time and push it away from the f7 attack.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bx.note: Black recaptures toward the centre, opening lines for the c8-bishop and the queen.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.note: Black kicks the bishop and stops Bxc6 ideas, gaining space on the queenside.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.note: Black kicks the bishop to gain queenside space and free the c6-knight from the pin, so that ...d5 can follow to support the e4-knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O.note: Black castles too, finishing the king's safety. Both sides now manoeuvre slowly.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 d6 d4 exd4 cxd4.note: Black retreats the bishop to a safe square where it still aims at d4. White has the bigger centre; Black is solid and will develop with ...Nf6.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Bc5 O-O d6 c3 O.note: Black castles too. The usual slow Italian middlegame: both sides manoeuvre before a break like d4 or ...d5.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c.note: Black develops the last minor piece to e7 (f6 is taken by the queen) and gets ready to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4 B.note: Black grabs the e4-pawn with check. Black is a pawn up, but the queen is out early and the c7 fork is still in the air.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7 B.note: Black takes the knight and pins the e4-bishop to the king. Next ...dxe4 wins the bishop, leaving Black a piece up.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nxe5 d5 Bd3 Qe7 B.cue: Grab the loose knight in a way that pins White's bishop to the king.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5 d5 Bb5.note: Black blocks the check with a pawn that attacks the bishop, so it must move again. Black is a pawn up and well developed.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Ng5 d5 Bb5.cue: Block the check with a pawn that also attacks the bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O d3.note: Black copies again: e5 is solidly protected and the c8-bishop can come out, for example to g4.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4 O-O O-O d3.cue: Shore up your e-pawn with a pawn and free your light-squared bishop.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3.note: Black develops quietly and gets ready to castle. The knight on e4 is still held by the d5-pawn.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3.cue: Develop your dark-squared bishop modestly so you can castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-.note: Black develops the bishop to guard e5 and prepares to castle. Black's position is easy and active.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Be2 d5 exd5 Nxd5 O-.cue: Develop your kingside bishop so it also guards your e-pawn, then castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3 h6 Bxf6.note: Black recaptures with the bishop, keeping a healthy pawn structure and gaining the bishop pair.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Bg5 Be7 Nc3 h6 Bxf6.cue: A piece was taken: recapture with the piece that keeps your pawns healthy.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Bd6 O-.note: Black castles too, keeping the position symmetrical and solid. Next comes development of the queenside pieces.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 Bd3 d5 Nxe5 Bd6 O-.cue: Your king is still in the centre: get it safe.

e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 Nh6.note: The knight can't go to f6 because of e5, so it heads for f5 to add yet more pressure on d4.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.note: White wins the pawn back while developing the bishop, and is ready to castle.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e.note: White wins the pawn back, developing the bishop to an active square and getting ready to castle.

d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 d.note: White takes back the pawn and the bishop is active again.
d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 d.cue: Recapture the pawn you just lost.

d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Nc6 Bf.note: White opens the f1-bishop and supports d4, getting ready to develop the bishop and castle.

d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h.note: White keeps the pin by retreating along the same diagonal instead of giving up the bishop for the knight.
d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h.cue: Your bishop is attacked — retreat it but keep the pin.

e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb3.note: White's bishop moves to c2, aiming at the h7-pawn and Black's kingside. The e5-pawn keeps Black's knights off f6.
e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nb6 Bb3.cue: Your bishop is attacked again. Find a safe square where it points at Black's kingside.

e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6 N.note: White develops with tempo, hitting the queen. If Black takes on f3, White recaptures and Black's queen is still attacked.
e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5 Qxd5 d4 cxd4 cxd4 Nc6 N.cue: Develop a piece that attacks the enemy queen.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: White develops and prepares h5 plus Bd3 to trade off Black's good bishop.

e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4.note: White develops and prepares h5 plus Bd3 to trade off Black's good bishop.

e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 N.note: White moves the queen to a square that still eyes f7, so Nxd6+ remains a threat (after ...cxd6, Qxf7 is mate).
e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 N.cue: Your queen is attacked — move it where it still aims at f7.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bx.note: White wins back the pawn and gains time: the e5-pawn attacks the d6-knight, which must move.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bx.cue: Win back your pawn with a capture that also attacks Black's knight.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.note: White retreats to the a2-g8 diagonal, where the bishop aims at f7 and is hard to chase further.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1.cue: Your bishop is attacked — retreat it to a diagonal aimed at f7.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.note: White keeps the bishop on the diagonal toward f7 and d5, where it bothers Black's centre.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4.cue: Your bishop is attacked — move it to a safe square still aimed at Black's king side.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O.note: White puts the rook behind the e4-pawn: it protects e4 and supports a future d4 break, after which the e-file may open.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O O.cue: Bring a rook to the file where your centre pawn stands, to back it up.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c.note: White connects the queen to the bishop on e3, adds support on the dark squares, and prepares Nb5 ideas or castling queenside. Balanced, normal play.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Bc5 Be3 Qf6 c.cue: Bring the queen up one square to back up your bishop and get ready to castle.

e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4 B.note: White blocks the check while developing and getting ready to castle — and Nxc7+ forking king and rook is still threatened. White is giving a pawn for a big lead in development.
e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4 Qh4 Nb5 Bb4 B.cue: Block the check with a piece that develops and lets you castle next.
